Case reference: 2014005000.CaseDesc: On August 10, 2004, Louis Lathlin was reported missing to police by his wife. She told police the last time she saw him was on June 14, when he left The Pas for Winnipeg, Manitoba for a doctor's appointment on the 15th. He took only personal hygiene items and no clothing. He later called his wife and told her that he would be staying in Winnipeg as he had another appointment on Thursday. He called his wife on Saturday morning requesting money. His wife sent the money as requested, but by Tuesday it had not been claimed. Louis has a history of living on the streets and has ties to Edmonton where he spent years on the streets. He also has various medical issues. He is believed to be in Winnipeg of his own volition. Louis' whereabouts remain unknown.

Case reference: 2014002231.CaseDesc: On September 25, 1980, Heinz Gamper was seen for the last time when he went mountain climbing in Jasper National Park in Jasper, Alberta. Following this time, Heinz was scheduled to work, but he did not attend his scheduled shift.

Case reference: 2006012299.CaseDesc: On June 02, 1984, Andrew Grinnell, his brother, their cousin and a friend departed Sioux Lookout on a canoe trip on the Albany River. The party arrived in Fort Albany on July 18, 1984. At 6:00 p.m. that same day, the party decided to leave Fort Albany in an attempt to paddle to Moosonee via James Bay. The group had planned to go out onto James Bay with the tide and sail to Moosonee by lashing their canoes together. An intense storm engulfed the James Bay coastal area on July 23, 1984, and it is likely that the party perished on the Bay during this storm. Three victims were recovered in August 1984, twelve nautical miles North of the Moose River. Andrew's body has never been recovered.

Case reference: 2014003678.CaseDesc: Donald McKillop’s spouse reported him missing on June 21, 1960. When she returned home on June 20 after working away from the house, she discovered he had left. When she last spoke to him on June 19, Donald had made no mention of intending to leave their house for any reason.  He didn't take his wallet or any other personal items when he left. Donald walks with a limp and there is no indication that foul play is suspected in his disappearance.

James has not been located and is presumed drowned.

Case reference: 2008016999.CaseDesc: Meryl Newcombe and George Weeden were last seen and reported missing to the White River OPP on October 29, 1959.  The two men had been at a lodge operated by Meryl at Mile 107 of the CPR line, west of Chapleau, Ontario. Meryl and George had planned a hunting trip and both were last seen between mile marker 106 and 107 of the CPR line southeast of White River and west of Chapleau. A large- scale search was conducted at the time, and again the following Spring (1960). The search failed to locate them, and to this day, they have not been located. Case reference: 2016052751.CaseDesc: On August 4, 2016, Suchand Reddy Pingli was seen for the last time at his apartment in the Le Plateau-Mont-Royal District of Montreal, Quebec. Suchand suffers from health problems and has to take medication regularly. He is from India.

Case reference: 2012020138.CaseDesc: The 18 month old Yohanna went missing after the mother entrusted the custody of her daughter to her boyfriend while she was out of town for a few days. They all lived in the Saint Laurent area in Montreal. Upon her return to Montreal, the mother was told that her baby was in Washington with the boyfriend’s mother. She went to the United States to find her daughter, but could not locate her. Returning to Quebec, the mother alerted the police of her child’s disappearance. The boyfriend claimed then that the child drowned in the bathtub during the mother’s absence and that she had been buried before the mother’s return. He was questioned and then released due to lack of evidence.
